thesis: The speakers argue that the market is currently mispricing SaaS companies by treating them as a single stable category despite a disruptive shift where some businesses are tied to work AI can now perform while others serve as a pricing proxy for headcount. They contend that not every SaaS company will thrive in the next decade, requiring a transition from static database models to AI agents that can actually execute work, a change that involves significant risks and requires companies to prove their adaptability over time.
